matches.rationale: Both flag that Table 3's SNN position error of 0.02m (or 0.04m) versus the ANN is reported without uncertainty estimates, while Section 5.3 describes oscillatory behaviour, creating an inconsistency between claimed precision and observed reliability. The finding's emphasis on missing error bars and the contradiction between the numbers and the qualitative 'oscillatory' description matches the ground-truth issue exactly.

The ground-truth states that Equation (1) places the BC term inside the warm‑up indicator, zeroing the BC loss during warm‑up, which contradicts the stated purpose. The only finding on Equation (1) (pred_id 3) claims the indicator applies only to the Q‑term and not the BC term, which is a different scientific issue.

The ground-truth points to an asymmetry in seed/repetition reporting between Figure 4 (5 seeds, 20 runs) and the ablation study in Table 4. None of the supplied findings mention this reporting asymmetry.
The ground-truth focuses on an unsupported 2.1× improvement claim in the abstract. No finding discusses the 2.1× factor or the conflation of training speed and final performance.
The ground-truth is about misattributing the fast sigmoid approximation to reference [27]. No finding addresses this reference or the misattribution.
The ground-truth concerns missing safety/ethical discussion around real‑world drone crashes. No finding identifies any ethical or safety omission.
The ground-truth highlights promotional language in the abstract ('set to revolutionize', 'orders-of-magnitude'). No finding points out this rhetorical overstatement.

The ground-truth describes an inconsistency between the claim that the SNN does not need action history and the fact that the critic uses action history. None of the findings capture this specific cross‑section inconsistency.

Both identify that the text asserts BC and TD3BC fail to exceed −200 points, whereas Figure 4a shows them reaching approximately −100 to −150 (and BC possibly around 0), thus exaggerating the performance difference. This is the same data‑text inconsistency at the same location.
The ground-truth concerns the undefined derivative r′ in Equation (7). No finding mentions this equation or the missing definition.
The ground-truth points out a 3.3× difference in training epochs (1000 vs 300) that is not acknowledged, biasing the comparison. No finding discusses training epoch disparities.

The ground-truth criticizes the conflation of random gradient directions with beneficial exploration noise in Section 5.1. No finding mentions cosine similarity or an overinterpretation of gradient noise.
The ground-truth is about a misrepresented reference [18] regarding energy savings. No finding addresses this reference or the unsupported energy claim.
The ground-truth describes an unfair architectural comparison (ANN [64-64] vs SNN [256-128]) in Table 2. No finding highlights this architecture mismatch as cherry‑picking.

The ground-truth notes a mismatch between the abstract's general claim and the conclusion's admission of a guiding‑policy dependency. No finding identifies an abstract‑conclusion limitation discrepancy.
The ground-truth criticizes the conclusion's overstatement of theoretical advancement. No finding addresses this rhetorical exaggeration.
The ground-truth concerns the soft‑reset equation's physical implausibility and missing description. No finding mentions the reset mechanism or Equation (4).
The ground-truth flags missing schedule details in the curriculum (Table 5). None of the findings discuss the curriculum's interpolation or step triggers.

The ground-truth challenges the unsupported sim‑to‑real transfer claim and notes the oscillatory behavior as evidence against seamless transfer. No finding addresses the sim‑to‑real claim or lack of domain randomization.
The ground-truth points out implausibly low error bars for completely failed configurations in Table 4. No finding mentions this statistical implausibility.
